summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Loop & No-Progress Detection; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: **In scope:** how agent runtimes detect that an agent is looping or making no progress. This covers the detector's parts (signal, comparison key, window, threshold, and response), the invariants it relies on, and where it fails. **Out of scope:** sibling guardrails (budget/cost caps as a discipline, timeouts, human-in-the-loop, retries and backoff), the parent domain, and text-generation degeneration as a decoding topic. Where a hard cap such as `max_turns` appears below, it appears only as the backstop part of a loop detector.

**Caveats:** - The OpenHands `stuck.py` source returned 404 at both `All-Hands-AI` and `OpenHands` raw paths. OpenHands thresholds therefore come from its official SDK docs. - The Gemini CLI source was read through an automated summarizer, so verify its constant values against the file before quoting them as exact. - A Claude Code issue reporting a "false positive" (anthropics/claude-code#93294) was excluded. It was closed as needs-repro and does not show that loop detection was the cause.

33. False positives on legitimate waiting: in OpenHands issue #5355 (2024-12-01), agents that repeatedly slept while polling a long-running process were killed with "agent got stuck in a loop". The issue closed as stale with no recorded fix. https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/5355 34. Recovery hazard: in OpenHands, once an agent was flagged stuck, the user could not recover it. A reviewer asked for the stuck state to reset on new user messages and for the detector to look only at agent actions. The fix PR #5500 was closed without merging. https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/pull/

35. Agent frameworks use model-emitted progress signals to decide whether to continue. A 2026 study found that the accuracy of these reports drops during mid-task execution, and that newer models are over-cautious near completion — https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08589 36. That study concludes that agent systems "should not depend solely on model state reports" to control task flow. An external detector is still required — https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08589

**Out of scope:** sibling guardrails such as cost or budget limits, timeouts, human-in-the-loop, self-reflection as a general technique, and termination or verification design. It also leaves out the parent domain. Two precursors appear only as context: classical cycle detection and token-level repetition during decoding. They are not researched further.

Above that, the outer loop runs: the Orchestrator reflects, updates the task ledger, revises the plan, and restarts the inner loop. https://arxiv.org/html

35. No general algorithm decides halting for all program–input pairs. A deterministic machine with finite memory must eventually halt or repeat a configuration, so for such machines, detecting a repeated state is complete. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halting_problem 36. *Inference, not sourced:* an LLM agent is not a closed deterministic finite-state system. It samples, and its tools change external state. So a repeated action does not prove a loop (the world may have changed), and a loop does not guarantee a repeated action (paraphrase, a different argument, or oscillation). Exact-match det
